To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of immobilized glucose-isomerase (IG) in a mixture with Aspergillus biomass allowed to increase the fructooligosacharides (FOS)-production yield and decrease the glucose/fructos (G/F) in the reaction mixture.

the use of immobilized glucose–fructose isomerase in the production of fructooligosacrharides by the fungus Aspergillus niger N74 allowed to increase the fructooligosacharides production yield and to reduce the glucose/fructose ratio in the reaction mixture.
the kinetic model for FOS production from sucrose by A. oryzae cells is proposed and the effect of IGI in FOS production was modeled.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modeling of a complex reaction system, where a fungus and an enzyme were simultaneously involved in a reaction mixture.
the development of a mathematical kinetic model that can be used to optimize the production of FOS by A. oryzae.
the modeling of the kinetics for FOS production, which can help to understand the reaction mechanism and the effects of the different parameters on FOS production, as well as to optimize the process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of IGI as a biocatalyst in FOS production by A. oryzae is not a viable strategy for improving the FOS production, but it could be a strategy to reduce the residual glucose in the reaction mixture.

the use of immobilized glucose-isomerase in the fructooligosacharides production process using A. oryzae biomass, is an interesting alternative to reduce the G/F ratio and to increase the Fos production yield.   1
the presence of ICI in the reaction mixture favored the reduction in the G/F ratio and the FOSY yield was increased in 1.5 % at bench scale, which is an improvement in the production of FOS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed kinetic model could be used as a useful tool for the design of a continuous reactor for the bioconversion to FOS using either free or immobilized fungal cells.
the proposed kinetic model can be used for the prediction of FOS production yield in the presence of IGF, and the presence of the IGI can be considered to improve FOS production yield.
the kinetic model developed in this study can be used to predict the behavior of the FOS production system using either free cells of As. oryzae or immobilized cells of As.oryzae and IGI.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the kinetic model developed for the FOS production process can be applied in the design and optimization of the process.
it is feasible to model the production of FOS by A. oryzae using the proposed kinetic models.
the use of a mathematical model can be used as a tool to evaluate the effect of IGI on FOS production and to determine the optimum reaction time.
